_doc: The ONE registry of actions the read-only ✦ chat may offer as buttons. Both sides read this file: srv/prompts.py teaches Claude the menu from it, and src/chatActions.ts dispatches a clicked button from it — so the taught vocabulary and the wired dispatch can never drift. The chat itself stays read-only (Read/Grep/Glob); an action is a PROPOSAL the viewer renders and the human clicks to run against an endpoint that already exists.

actions.label: What merges next?
actions.describe: Read-only navigation: returns the LIVE, server-computed merge-readiness of this branch's forest — which branches have an open PR vs are clear to merge into main right now, in canonical order. This is state you CANNOT infer from the diff (it checks real PRs), so offer it whenever the user asks what comes next / which branch lands next / where this sits in the merge order — even if you can sketch the structure yourself, the button adds the current PR + mergeable status you don't have. params: none.

actions.label: Mark as forest trunk
actions.describe: Mark this approved-but-unmerged branch as its forest's trunk anchor: the viewer then treats it like main — it stops reading as 'behind main', and its descendants measure/rebase against IT until it merges. Offer when a branch is approved, isn't merging today, and others build on it. params: none.

actions.label: Catch me up
actions.describe: Read-only recall: summarize where this branch sits — its purpose, what parent..branch changes, what's still unblessed, and its place in the forest. Offer when the user asks 'remind me what this is' or 'where were we'. It sends itself as a normal chat message (reuses the ✦ chat), so the answer streams below. params: none.
actions.message: Catch me up on this branch: its purpose, what it changes versus its parent, what's still unblessed, and where it sits in the forest.

actions.label: Set branch purpose
actions.describe: Save a one-line purpose as this branch's git description. Offer ONLY when the branch appears to have no purpose yet, or the user is explicitly asking about the branch's intent — never as a generic follow-up to an unrelated answer. params: text (the one-line purpose in plain language — what the branch does, not how it's coded).

params.name: text
params.desc: the one-line purpose in plain language — what the branch does, not how it's coded

actions.label: Bless this file
actions.describe: Mark the file under review as blessed. Offer only in a file-scoped chat when the file's change looks correct and complete.

actions.label: Squash to working tree
actions.describe: Collapse the branch's parent..branch history into unstaged working-tree changes (Phil writes the commit himself). Offer when the branch has messy WIP commits worth flattening.

actions.label: Prep to merge
actions.describe: Squash the whole branch into one clean, formatted commit for a single-commit PR. Offer when the branch is ready to ship.

actions.label: Restack onto origin/main
actions.describe: Rebase this unpublished root branch onto fresh origin/main. Offer when the branch has fallen behind main.
